In which of the following equilibria, Kp and Kc are NOT equal?
(1)
5(g) 3(g) 2(g)PCl PCl Cl +
(2)
2(g) 2(g) (g)H I 2HI+
(3)
(g) 2 (g) 2(g) 2(g)CO H O CO H++
(4)
(g) 2(g) 2(g)2BrCl Br Cl +
Thermodynamics
subject: Chemistry
b6_reason: Kp = Kc(RT)^(delta n), so they differ only when the gaseous mole count changes; only PCl5 -> PCl3 + Cl2 has delta n = +1.
b6_working: Option 1 PCl5(g) <-> PCl3(g) + Cl2(g): delta n = 2-1 = +1, Kp != Kc. Option 2 H2+I2 <-> 2HI: delta n = 2-2 = 0. Option 3 CO+H2O <-> CO2+H2: delta n = 0. Option 4 2BrCl <-> Br2+Cl2: delta n = 0.
b6_note: All four options are badly mangled by extraction - subscripts and state labels are interleaved ahead of the formulae and the equilibrium arrows are lost (e.g. '5(g) 3(g) 2(g)PCl PCl Cl +'). The reactions are still recoverable as PCl5/PCl3+Cl2, H2+I2/2HI, CO+H2O/CO2+H2 and 2BrCl/Br2+Cl2, and only the first changes gaseous moles, but the options should be re-extracted before this key is trusted.
